loop/need: Some questions take more than one call. Ask for the weather in the capital of Peru, and the model must first find the capital.
loop/first: So it writes a call: search for the capital of Peru. The program runs it and appends the result, Lima. That was turn one.
loop/second: Then the program runs the model again. With Lima in view, turn two's call is weather of Lima, and back comes nineteen degrees, cloudy.
loop/answer: On turn three the model writes no call, only the answer. A turn that ends in an answer instead of a call ends the loop.
loop/limit: In case the model never stops calling, the program also sets a step limit, here ten turns. A model run in this loop is an agent; the ReAct paper described it in 2022.
grow/p: Every turn makes the context longer. Say the prompt, the question with the tools it may use, takes thirty tokens.
grow/t1: Turn one adds a call of five tokens and a result of fifteen: fifty. Turn two adds twenty more: seventy.
grow/gen: Nothing is removed. After any turn, call it turn t, the context is the prompt plus every call and result so far: thirty plus twenty times t.
reread/prefill: Each turn starts with a prefill: one pass that reads the whole context before the model writes.
reread/plain: Done plainly, every turn prefills from scratch: thirty tokens on turn one, fifty on turn two, and seventy on turn three, where it writes the answer.
reread/sum: That is a hundred and fifty tokens, a sum of lengths that each grow. Every extra turn costs more than the one before.
reread/same: But appending tokens never changes the keys and values of the tokens before them: the causal mask sees to that. So keep them, as the KV cache does.
reread/new: Then each turn prefills only what is new. The call's keys and values were stored as the model wrote it, so only the result is new: fifteen tokens.
reread/cache: Thirty, then fifteen, then fifteen: sixty instead of a hundred and fifty. Keeping the earlier context like this is called prefix caching.
try/p1: Try one: a prompt of forty tokens, then two calls of five, each with a result of ten, then the answer. How many tokens are prefilled without a cache?
try/a1: The three turns read forty, then fifty-five, then seventy: a hundred and sixty-five.
try/a2: With the cached prefix, they read forty, then ten, then ten: sixty.
